quotes: "PAH enzyme activity was reduced in the presence of DNAJC12 mutations." (Anikster et al. 2017, PMID 28132689); "At saturation, four DNAJC12 monomers bind and stabilize the PAH tetramer, protecting it from aggregation and lowering the L-Phe concentration necessary for substrate-induced activation" (Tai et al. 2026, PMID 42497073)
species_evidence: human (patients with biallelic DNAJC12 variants); recombinant human proteins
reading: a co-chaperone that keeps phenylalanine hydroxylase stable and active, so its loss lowers PAH activity (hyperphenylalaninemia in the patients)

quotes: "DNAJC12 binding stabilizes both TH and the variant TH-p.R202H, associated with TH deficiency" and "This binding delays their time-dependent aggregation in an Hsp70-independent manner, while preserving TH activity and feedback regulatory inhibition by dopamine." (Tai et al. 2025, PMID 40113792); "DNAJC12, which encodes a heat shock co-chaperone family member that interacts with phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan hydroxylases" (Anikster et al. 2017, PMID 28132689)
species_evidence: recombinant human TH; human (patients with dopamine and serotonin deficiency)
reading: the co-chaperone stabilizes tyrosine hydroxylase, the rate-limiting enzyme of dopamine synthesis. One knockout mouse study found the TH and TPH2 proteins unchanged while brain monoamines fell: "while tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and tryptophan hydroxylase 2 (TPH2) expression remained unchanged" (Wang et al. 2025, PMID 39923104), so the edge stands for the enzyme's activity, which the graph's protein state carries, not its amount.

quotes: "CblC (or MMACHC) is a processing chaperone that catalyzes an early step in this trafficking pathway. CblC removes the upper axial ligand of cobalamin derivatives, forming an intermediate in the pathway that is subsequently converted to the active cofactor derivatives." (Mascarenhas et al. 2020, PMID 32457044); "It catalyzes the glutathione (GSH)-dependent dealkylation of alkylcobalamins and the reductive decyanation of cyanocobalamin." (Li et al. 2017, PMID 28442570); "Transduction of wild-type MMACHC into immortalized cblC fibroblast cell lines corrected the cellular phenotype." (Lerner-Ellis et al. 2006, PMID 16311595)
species_evidence: recombinant human protein; human cblC fibroblasts
reading: Human-GEM's aquacob(III)alamin reduction (MAR08613) is the graph's one step from an incoming cob(III)alamin to cytosolic cob(II)alamin, the intermediate both cofactors are made from, and it has no catalyst; MMACHC is the enzyme of that step. The abstracts name cyanocobalamin, alkylcobalamins and nitrocobalamin as its substrates, not aquacobalamin, so the edge stands for the processing step rather than for the exact substrate

quotes: "MMAA regulates the incorporation of the cofactor adenosylcobalamin (AdoCbl), generated from the MMAB adenosyltransferase, into the destination enzyme methylmalonyl-CoA mutase (MUT)." (Plessl et al. 2017, PMID 28497574); "in the cofactor forms methyl-Cbl and adenosyl-Cbl, is required for the function of the essential enzymes methionine synthase and methylmalonyl-CoA mutase, respectively" (Fettelschoss et al. 2017, PMID 28572511)
species_evidence: human (cblA patients and their fibroblasts; recombinant human proteins)
reading: Human-GEM names adenosylcobalamin cobamide-coenzyme; its mitochondrial pool (MAM01600m) is the product of MMAB's adenosyltransferase reactions and fed no enzyme, and BRENDA's cofactor rows reach MMUT only as Mg2+ and hydrochloride. Methionine synthase already has methylcobalamin as a cofactor (BRENDA)
